introduction.en: The International Finance Corporation (IFC), established in 1956, is the largest global development institution focused exclusively on the private sector in developing countries. It operates as a member of the World Bank Group.
introduction.hi: The International Finance Corporation (IFC), established in 1956, is the largest global development institution focused exclusively on the private sector in developing countries. It operates as a member of the World Bank Group.

body.en: IFC plays a critical role by providing debt and equity financing to private enterprises, which helps in creating jobs and fostering innovation. In India, the IFC has been instrumental in supporting renewable energy projects, strengthening the financial sector, and promoting public-private partnerships (PPPs). By mobilizing third-party capital, the IFC bridges the funding gap for large-scale infrastructure projects that might otherwise struggle to attract private investment. Furthermore, its advisory services help local firms adopt international environmental, social, and governance (ESG) standards.

conclusion.en: By catalyzing private investment and promoting sustainable business practices, the IFC remains a vital partner for India in achieving its long-term economic growth and development goals.
